dedupe_keys.name: simulation data on evacuation shelter location and water access after an earthquake small coastal town

description: This dataset holds the data and code for a framework that analyses water network resilience together with evacuation behaviour, shelter location and service availability at critical facilities after a disaster. It was published on Mendeley Data on 17 April 2026 by Jason Poff to accompany a paper on evaluating evacuation shelter location impacts on water access during seismic events. Probabilistic damage scenarios from a 250-year earthquake on the water distribution network of a small coastal town were run for 72 hours of hydraulic performance with 10 possible shelter sites; average water availability differed by up to a factor of 2.6 between sites. Coverage: one small coastal town, not named in the record. Access: Mendeley Data download. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a single network and hazard level; the town and network source are not identified in the record. Simulation uses: choosing shelter sites and testing how evacuation-driven demand affects water supply to hospitals and other critical facilities. Related records: the Galveston testbed and the Onslow Community Resilience Testbed.
